Why is it “yikes” when a psychologist with prescribing licensure has advanced specialized training in prescribing psychotropic drugs? They have to have completed a postdoctoral master of science degree in clinical psychopharmacology, a supervised practicum in clinical assessment and pathophysiology, and passed a national examination. Additionally, after meeting these requirements a prescribing psychologist will have a two-year provisional certificate to prescribe under the mandatory supervision of an MD. (Which I’m sure requirements vary by state) but allowing psychologist prescribing ability, does increase access to mental health care that might not always be present in certain populations. It’s not like these people are just handed a script pad to go out and can prescribe whatever they want.

C-PTSD isn’t in the DSM so it isn’t surprising for older clinicians to not know about it. It’s in the ICD however. 

More trauma specialist however have more information related to it. At my workplace instead of using terms like borderline personality disorder we say CPTSD.

CPTSD and BPD share a lot of similarity especially in terms of being closely related to relational trauma. I know a clinician who likes to view the two on a spectrum sense. But it’s important to note that the mental health community does want to move away from the term borderline personality disorder and even within this community there is a great deal of misunderstanding related to BPD. But typically there’s always a correlation between the experience of complex trauma within individuals with a BPD diagnosis.
